text:
Legendary Zimbabwean footballers who are back home
Several Zimbabwean footballers who built their careers in South Africa have returned home, bringing leadership to develop the game.
Several Zimbabwean footballers built successful careers in South Africa’s Premier Soccer League before eventually returning home.
From pioneers who opened doors for others to modern stars who thrilled PSL fans, these players left a lasting mark across the border.
Here are five Zimbabwean footballers who have returned home after making their names in South African football.
Peter Ndlovu: Zimbabwe’s greatest footballer
Peter Ndlovu is widely regarded as one of Zimbabwe’s greatest footballers.
Although he spent much of his career in England, he also had a memorable stint in South Africa with Mamelodi Sundowns.
Ndlovu later has returned to Zimbabwe as team manager at Scottland FC.
Ndlovu, who was recently serving as team manager at Sundowns, took up the same role at the reigning Zimbabwean Premier Soccer League champions.
Willard Katsande – Midfield maestro
Willard Katsande became a cult hero at Kaizer Chiefs, where he spent nearly a decade dominating midfield battles.
After leaving the PSL, Katsande returned to Zimbabwe and got involved in football and business ventures while mentoring young players.
Last year, ZIFA appointed the former footballer to its Ad hoc Committee on Diaspora and Global Interaction.
Katsande has taken the next step in his football career after being appointed head coach of Rangers FC.
Khama Billiat – Star forward and celebrated footballer
Khama Billiat enjoyed enormous success in South Africa, especially during his time at Mamelodi Sundowns, where he won multiple league titles and continental honours.
The former Zimbabwe national football team star later returned to Zimbabwe, where his move back to the local league attracted massive attention from fans.
Billiat is currently playing for the reigning Zimbabwean PSL champions, Scotland FC.
Knowledge Musona – “Smiling Assassin” and prolific striker
Nicknamed “The Smiling Assassin,” Knowledge Musona also played in South Africa early in his career with Kaizer Chiefs.
After playing in Europe and Asia, Musona eventually returned home to join Khama Billiat at Scottland FC.
This marked a major moment for Zimbabwean football as one of the country’s biggest modern stars came back.
Esrom Nyandoro – Respected midfield general and loyal footballer
Esrom Nyandoro spent more than a decade at Mamelodi Sundowns, becoming one of the club’s most respected footballers.
He recently launched the Esrom Nyandoro Foundation, which aims to support over 200 underprivileged children in both Zimbabwe and South Africa.
This month, Nyandoro was officially announced as a talent scout for the Zimbabwean club Kwekwe United to assist in their professional growth.
